capability: Coin-flip answers and money go to a person
title: Coin flips go to a person.

hook.picture: Close on the whale beside a spinning coin on the line. The coin lands on its edge, wobbles, and falls 'yes'. A payout card slides down the line.
hook.words: It was basically a coin toss.

problem_in_viewer_words.body: It was fifty-fifty, and it paid out anyway.

why_it_keeps_happening.picture: Pull back: a row of spinning coins. Each lands near the middle and is read as yes. Three payouts slide, every 2 beats, then 1, then ½.
why_it_keeps_happening.words: A coin toss gets read as yes.

stakes.body: Money leaves on a coin toss, and no one can undo it. The customer loses trust and the money doesn't come back.

solution_hint: If it's a coin toss, ask a person.

metaphor.body: A meter with a shaded middle band sits on the line. Answers inside the band, and any card that moves money, are lifted out to the whale. Only clear answers on small things keep flowing.

steps.picture: The coin becomes a ring meter with a shaded middle band. A clear, high answer passes straight through the gate.
steps.words: Clear answers pass on their own.

steps.picture: Push-in (z 1.28): an answer lands in the middle band. The gate lifts it off the line and hands it up to the whale.
steps.words: Near the middle? It goes to you.
steps.sound: The ring lifts up a third

steps.picture: A payout card arrives, even with a clear answer. A copper pin on it sends it up to the whale too.
steps.words: Money always goes to a person.

steps.picture: The whale reads the two held cards, decides, and drops a tick for each.

real_case.claim: The jev-elder pinned contracts say: "Mid-band ~0.5 is a coin flip. Escalate." and "Irreversible / money → human."

honest_limit.picture: Still. A wrong answer lands high on the meter, far from the band. It passes straight through and the payout slides. A copper flag rises behind it.
honest_limit.words: A sure wrong answer skips the person.

not_this.body: High score is not the same as right.

ending_pattern.body: The coin caught mid-air: the same coin toss no longer decides the payout, because the whale catches it before it lands.
ending_pattern.callback: The coin that tipped the payout in bar 1 is caught by the whale before it lands.

end_belief.body: Coin toss? Hand it to a person.

score_self.reason: The coin flip is an everyday symbol, the pain is visceral, and the rule is sourced verbatim. Risk: the coin is a new prop beyond the lexicon (drawn as the ring meter), and "escalating" is a stiff word.
